lore.title: The World of Etheria
lore.subtitle: A land forged by forgotten gods
paragraphs: Etheria was created when the ancient gods awoke from their thousand-year slumber. In their fury, they shattered the world into floating islands, each a battlefield where mortals and divine beings fight for increasingly scarce resources.

Today, three main factions dominate the landscape: the Aurelion, guardians of the golden light; the Shadowmere, masters of intrigue and shadows; and the Frostborne, northern warriors who worship ice crystals. You will choose your side.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.subtitle: Change history of Conquest of Etheria

added: [CORE] Full game v1 audit: technical report of current game functions and prioritized proposals.
Expanded domain test coverage for resources, configurable queues, world terrain, and bot decision engine.
[GAMEPLAY] Unified reports center: all battle, spy, season, and quest notifications in one inbox with unread counter.
Initial quests: complete missions per city, claim configurable rewards, and receive reports on completion.
Public market: create and accept trade offers from the Market building with server-validated resource exchange.
Scouting: send spies to gather intel on cities and barbarian camps with estimated intelligence reports.
Alliance objectives: contribute resources to shared goals with visible progress and temporary alliance effects.
Reports now accessible from the messages modal with shared unread badge for mail and reports.
Market opens from the Market building instead of the sidebar.
Barbarian camps can be scouted from their modal to generate intel reports without revealing fog.
Extended dual persistence for MatecitoDB/PostgreSQL with new collections and Prisma models.
Bots can now trade in the market, contribute to alliance objectives, and scout enemies using real game services.
Quests now loaded from domain config for easier balancing and future quest additions.
[WORLD] Season change reports: the system emits notifications on season and phase changes visible in the HUD.
fixed: [CORE] Passive production no longer reduces resources when lastResourceUpdate is ahead of current time.
Active queue slots are now properly capped by the configured maximum regardless of environment values.

added: Live World Map: Real-time visualization of armies and trade caravans with physical movement.
Seasonal Weather Layer: Visual effects for snow, autumn, and summer applied dynamically to the map.
Fog of War System: Progressive map discovery around your city.
Advanced Bot AI: Bots now attack players (respecting protection), trade with each other, and hunt barbarians.
Interactive Radial Menu: A new quick way to interact with the world map.
Bots now use the exact same city functions as players for authentic QA.
New public landing page with dark fantasy design, animated hero, and features section.
Automated changelog blog that reads directly from the version history.
Shared public layout with consistent Navbar and Footer.
Game access moved to /play route to separate marketing from gameplay.
Visual redesign of Login and Register pages with glassmorphism style.

fixed: Fixed winter pressure calculation: troops now consume food based on real elapsed time, preventing instant desertion.
Removed double food penalty in winter that was draining resources too fast.
Improved production accuracy: buildings now generate 1-3 extra units/hour after fixing rounding.
changed: Season effects are now configurable and loaded from config files.
Rebalanced building production curve: high-level upgrades (15-20) are now more cost-effective.
Optimized performance: resource updates now batch-load data instead of querying one by one.
added: Visible season system: spring, summer, autumn and winter with effects on production and the map.
Barbarian camps on the world map with visible army composition and rewards.
Barbarian camp attack system: select troops, attack and earn loot.
Barbarian attack alerts: urgent banner with countdown when a camp approaches your city.
Winter pressure: your troops consume food in winter; if supplies run out, they desert or lose combat power.
Camp scaling: surviving camps level up over time, becoming more dangerous.
Climate zones: the north and mountains suffer harsher winters; the south and coast are milder.
Simulation bot system for automated gameplay testing.
City ranking by Power accessible from the sidebar.
technical: Vitest test suite with 21 tests for winterPressure and production.
Config refactor: seasonEffects, cityBaseConfig, battleConfigData extracted to dedicated files.
Persistence diagnostics in barbarian spawn with DB error validation.

added: Alliance system: create or join alliances, manage roles, edit public description and sign peace treaties.
Player mail with unread badge from the sidebar.
Real-time chat with Global and Alliance channels in the bottom dock.
Immersive bottom dock: construction queue, active research and chat unified.
changed: Resource generation now applies technology bonuses and alliance peace effects.
Combat and training consistently use technology modifiers.
Village actions (upgrade, train, research) now use real backend mutations.
World map with continuous terrain: castles positioned directly on city coordinates.
Tower as the only defensive structure (wall removed from catalog).
fixed: Technology modifiers no longer lose global unit bonuses.
Combat no longer applies defender defensive bonuses to the attacker.
Training cancellation refunds respect the actual reduced cost.
Authentication system with HTTP-only sessions and remember me support.

added: Technology tree: 22 researches across 3 categories (Economy, Military, Defense).
Two exclusive specialization branches: Siege Mastery vs Cavalry Mastery.
Real combat bonuses: attack, HP, defense, speed and armor penetration per unit type.
Wall and Tower now impact combat: wall increases defensive HP, tower deals damage per round.
Unit unlocks: Cavalry, Siege and Spy require specific technologies.
Research panel with visual cards, prerequisites and completion timer.
changed: Unit stats are now calculated dynamically with technology bonuses.
Research queue is processed between training and resource ticks.

added: Full battle system: attack other cities, earn loot and receive combat reports.
Battle panel with 3 tabs: Attack, Reports and Active (with live timers).
HP-based combat model: each unit has hit points and armor penetration.
5 unit types with distinct roles: Warrior (tank), Archer (damage), Cavalry (fast), Siege (destroys walls), Spy (scouting).
changed: Procedural sprites for 13 building types with dark fantasy theme.
Complete frontend-backend integration: auto city management, real-time polling.
Resource bar with local calculation between server syncs.

added: Game engine with 50x50 tilemap, panoramic camera and click-to-build.
10 initial buildings: Town Hall, Barracks, Stable, Farm, Gold Mine, Sawmill, Quarry, Alliance Center, Library, Warehouse.
5 resources: Gold, Wood, Stone, Food, Gems with passive generation.
Construction and military training queue system.
Attack system with travel time between cities.
Offline progression: resources are calculated based on elapsed time.
HUD overlay with resource bar and building menu in React.
technical: Monorepo architecture with Turborepo + pnpm workspaces.
Backend: Hono API with Clean Architecture.
Migration from PostgreSQL/Prisma to matecito.dev document DB.
Building and unit configs stored in DB (310 records).
Shared package with Zod schemas for type contracts.

added: [AUDIO] Ambient music system with Web Audio API, 10 medieval-fantasy .ogg tracks, random playback with 30-90s pauses.
[NOTIFICATIONS] Incoming attack alerts: defender gets immediate report with ETA and troop composition when attacked.
[NOTIFICATIONS] Spy detection: 15% + TOWERx5% + SPY_NETWORK chance to detect enemy spies near your city.
[UI] Redesigned Barracks/Stable modal with unit stats (Atk/Def/HP/Speed/Carry/AP), quantity presets, and costs.
[UI] Redesigned Library modal with category tabs, researched-only filter, and Active Bonuses summary panel.
[UI] Battle reports now visible in the Messages modal under the Reports tab alongside game reports.
[UI] SeasonHUD redesign: shows season modifiers, intensity bar, time remaining, and winter pressure warning.
[BOTS] Complete AI overhaul: 20+ improvements including defense logic, spy intelligence, trade only to allies, seasonal adaptation, bot memory, and more.
fixed: [UI] Library research panel was broken (typo ACADEMY instead of LIBRARY).
[UI] Barracks modal did not show trained unit counts.
[i18n] ~20 missing translation keys added (mail compose, battle selectTroops, army stats, etc.).
[i18n] Fixed dot-notation issue in changelog version keys causing raw key display on landing.
[BOTS] Market accept now includes fee. Trade no longer sends resources to enemies. Consecutive loss recovery.
changed: [WORLD] Unit speeds rebalanced: Warrior 60→160, Cavalry 120→280, Trade 100→200, etc. Visual travel cap removed.
[WORLD] Terrain overlay disabled on world map.

added: [CORE] Configurable sequential queues
Construction, training, and research now support up to 3 pending slots per city.
Only 1 slot runs actively by default; following slots advance when the previous finishes.
Slot limits and concurrency are configuration-driven (no hardcoded gameplay values).
[UI] Persistent right queue panel
/play shows construction, training, and knowledge in one always-visible right panel.
Each queue item includes a cancel button with a 50% resource refund.
[WORLD] Village map asset
Player and bot cities in /mapa now use a fortified village sprite.
[BOTS] Living player simulation
Bots can recover from critical resources, prioritize economy, and keep decision memory.
Bots can create alliances, join alliances, chat, and send diplomatic messages.
changed: [BOTS] AI aligned with the queue engine
Bots can fill pending slots using the same city actions as players.
Bot simulation runs on the compatible data layer respecting PostgreSQL/MatecitoDB.
[UI] Simplified game sidebar
Duplicate queues removed from the left sidebar and bottom dock.
fixed: [EDITOR] World terrain mask
Painting plains is now visible in the map editor overlay.
The brush covers grid edges more reliably.
The editor camera can pan with extra margin for panel-covered edges.

added: [UNITS] 3 new units + full rebalance: Pikeman, Crossbowman, Catapult. Warrior/Archer buffed, Siege nerfed.
[UNITS] Barracks now trains all unit types (7 units). Stable only Cavalry.
[SPY] Spy rebalance: city scout returns home (lost if detected). Camp scout always lost. Better intel with numeric ranges.
[SPY] Detection base 15%→10%. SPY_NETWORK gives counter-intel (-5% detection). Spy trainable from lv1 Barracks.
[UI] Active Buffs Panel below SeasonHUD: icons with hover tooltips showing effect, source, and remaining time.
[UI] Attack modal from world map: select troops with +/-1/+10, see total cost, send attack directly.
[UI] Redesigned Barracks/Library modals: unit stats, quantity presets, category tabs, active bonuses.
[UI] Battle reports now visible in Messages modal under Reports tab.
[POWER] Power system: tech bonuses apply to unit stats, HP+AP in formula, alliance column + breakdown tooltip in ranking.
[BOTS] Bot IA overhaul: 20+ improvements including defense, spy intel, trade to allies, seasonal adaptation, memory.
changed: [BOTS] Attack visibility: cooldowns reduced (global 45min, attack 10-30min). Bots can attack bots. Max distance 140.
[BALANCE] Travel speeds rebalanced (Warrior 160, Cavalry 280, Trade 200). Visual 8min cap removed.
[UI] SeasonHUD redesign: shows resource modifiers, intensity bar, remaining time, winter pressure.
[UI] Attack troops reduced: 50%→30% (MILITARIST 40%).
fixed: [i18n] Dot-notation bug in changelog version keys (v0_2_2 format). ~30 missing keys added.
[i18n] SeasonHUD fully translated EN/ES.
[UI] ResourceBar no longer stretches full width next to SeasonHUD.
[UI] Library modal broken (ACADEMY→LIBRARY).
[UI] Barracks did not show trained units.
[BOTS] Market accept now includes fee. Trade only to allies.

added: [GAME] Quick navigation bar at the bottom to jump between your village, map, messages, alliance and rankings without getting lost.
[GAME] Improved build queue that repositions automatically so it doesn't cover your navigation buttons.
[GAME] Screen edges respected on phones with notch or bottom bar — nothing gets covered anymore.
[GAME] Active bonuses now visible by tapping their icons — no more mouse-only tooltips.
changed: [GAME] Side menu replaced by the new bottom bar on phones — everything within thumb's reach.
[GAME] Improved windows: larger close buttons, full-screen adaptation without overflow, and rounded corners that adjust automatically.
[GAME] Better village view on your phone — you can now zoom out a bit more to see everything at a glance.
[GAME] Notifications repositioned so they don't overlap with the bottom buttons.
fixed: [GAME] Window content that used to look cramped on phones now displays neatly and legibly.
[GAME] Buff info that only showed on mouse hover now also works when you tap with your finger.
[GAME] Fair winter: cities no longer become corrupted when entering their first winter with troops. A bug caused food to vanish and the city to become unplayable.
[GAME] Barbarians across the map: the north, center, and south now have barbarian camps. Previously 3 out of 7 zones had zero activity.
[GAME] Advanced storage now works: the technology that promised to increase your storage capacity actually does so now. It had no effect before.
[GAME] Winter with personality: winter now hits harder in the north (+35%) and lighter in the south (-30%), matching each region's climate.

human.name: Humans
human.description: Versatile and diplomatic. They adapt to any terrain with balanced production and trade bonuses.
human.lore: When the First Sun illuminated Etheria, humans were the first to raise walls. Natural diplomats and merchants, they forge alliances where others see enemies. Their gold flows like rivers and their armies, though not the strongest, are the best organized.

elf.name: Elves
elf.description: Masters of the forest and the bow. They produce more wood and food, and their archers are lethal.
elf.loreTitle: The Children of the Eternal Forest
elf.lore: Deep in the Eternal Forest, elves sing to the trees and they respond with fruit and endless wood. Their archers see in darkness and their arrows never miss. They prefer diplomacy, but their archer is feared throughout Etheria.

orc.name: Orcs
orc.description: Brutal warriors born for battle. They produce more stone and their units are tougher.
orc.lore: From the Broken Mountains rose the orcs, forged in fire and blood. They know neither fear nor defeat. Every orc is a warrior, every village a stronghold. They produce stone as they breathe and their armies do not stop until enemy walls crumble.

dwarf.name: Dwarves
dwarf.description: Unmatched forgers. They extract gold and stone faster, and their defenses are impenetrable.
dwarf.lore: Beneath the Eternal Mountains, dwarves have struck the anvil since before the surface realms existed. None extract gold and stone like them. Their defenses are legend — a single dwarven tower withstands what ten human walls cannot. They prefer peace, but in war they are unstoppable.
